seal.statement: Remove every production-reachable legacy consensus runtime and every active accommodation surface, leaving the raft-rs semantic operation port and runtime owner as Lagrange's only consensus implementation. MessageGroupService must construct the raft-rs port with durable local consensus state, derive committed membership from ConfState, publish role and leader from semantic status/events, propose and apply commands through the port, and restart without losing term, vote, or configuration. Every live RaftGroup and RaftReplicaBase consumer must either migrate to that boundary or be deleted when unreachable; process-level provider selection, distributed-harness provider vocabulary, migration/spike rollback tooling, the legacy dependency and implementation, legacy-only tests, and current documentation must be removed. A fixed-scope checker must reject case-insensitive legacy implementation references in filenames and contents across active surfaces while excluding only historical solve evidence. Before another five-node run, focused witnesses must prove message-group formation, proposal/commit, membership, restart, any retained generic/WASM consensus path, and zero active references.

MG R3 migration decisions: (1) MG opens one raft-rs operation port over its own durable replica DB (dataDir/message-groups/<group>/<replica>.db via DataDirectoryManager; missing dbPath fails closed MISSING_DB_PATH, ':memory:' refused), BOOTSTRAP_MEMBERSHIP=genesisStamp(replicaIds), DEFER_ELECTION=deferElection||deferElectionUntilJoinConvergence. (2) Inbound accepts only raft-rs transport envelopes (port.step); native packet branch and join vote denial dropped (D2: raft-rs tallies only configuration voters). (3) Membership growth only via reserveAndAdmitGroupPeer from the services-cache projection on the leader, re-driven on CONF_CHANGE_APPLIED/LEADER; replicaIds stays the bootstrap hint list. (4) RESOLVE_PEER_ADDRESS callback resolves from unified/cache/bootstrap hints only and never reads status (status computation calls it: recursion hazard); live resolution for forwarding reads status.peers. (5) Committed apply dispatches on MESSAGE_GROUP_COMMAND_TYPE with an admission owner refusing unknown types before propose; unknown committed type throws. (6) Proposal routing: leader proposes via port (CORE_OK on append = legacy command() parity F7), non-leader forwards; retry only on retryable non-recovery answers; existing per-attempt deadline kept, not widened. (7) Timing via port.configureTick; join suppression = stopScheduling until completeJoinConvergence -> startScheduling.

MG behaviour parity notes: (F7) the leader's port.propose answers CORE_OK on append, matching the retired command() resolution point - commit is observed through the committed apply on every replica; (routing miss) a CORE_REFUSED proposal by a replica the port says no longer leads is retryable within the existing per-attempt deadline and maxAttempts (no widening); (resolver) the RESOLVE_PEER_ADDRESS callback is called while status is shaped, so it resolves from unified/cache/bootstrap hints only, flagged consensusResolution:true, never reading status (recursion hazard); (persistToRaftLog) the CDC tail mirror stays fire-and-forget as before; (reconcileRaftPeersFromCache) admits peers through reserveAndAdmitGroupPeer and no longer extends replicaIds, which stays the bootstrap hint list; (apply) an unknown committed command type throws (fails closed) and effect failures are reported, not swallowed; pre-candidate port events are not subscribed (no MG consumer).

R2 joiner bootstrap: a joining MG replica opens deferred (stopScheduling until completeJoinConvergence) from genesisStamp(replicaIds) where replicaIds includes itself and the existing members - a superset of the leader's committed ConfState. It cannot campaign while deferred; the leader's AddNode (reserveAndAdmitGroupPeer) plus append/snapshot converge the joiner's applied configuration to the leader's. Edge case, same as the partition template: a lone replica opened deferred and restarted with a larger committed configuration gets no scheduling until join convergence completes.

Formation simulator: the old-runtime staged cohort is replaced by a raft-rs operation-port cohort (test/simulation/formation-sim-consensus-cohort.js) over the virtual network, built through RaftRsWasmProvider.createPartitionPort with an in-memory replica database and the charging network time source. The seed opens as a lone GENESIS voter and campaigns once (the production lone-replica rule); a joiner is admitted the production partition-join way: the leader's BOOTSTRAP committed-membership read gives its COMMITTED stamp, every member reserves and admits it through raft-rs-group-membership-admission (only the leader proposes ADD_PEER; NOT_LEADER/deferred admissions are re-driven on LEADER and CONF_CHANGE_APPLIED as the message group does), and its participation gate holds scheduling until it applies its own admission. Leadership stays an outcome of the real core, never scenario data (that would breach the simulator's real-owner constraint and remove raft_protocol load). Caveat (owner decision O2 of the cutover investigation, not funded here): raft-rs election randomness is unseeded, so a scenario that starves a node past its election timeout is not byte-reproducible; the current scenario does not starve the seed (0 gaps at base). The calibration remains the old runtime's measurement; re-measuring it belongs to its own owner.

Formation simulator cross-run leak: with the old runtime's ~30 awaitCurrentProtocolIdle() owner contracts gone, the heartbeat interval's fire-and-forget sendHeartbeat()/runScheduledMembershipPublicationReconcileTick() chains (heartbeat-service-lifecycle-methods.js, not awaited, no owner idle contract) outlived the closing instant and ran inside the NEXT simulate(), where attribution refused them as UNBOUND PROVENANCE. The removed idle awaits had only been lending those chains microtask budget. Fix (runner only, following the production seed host's hostTurn owner contract in formation-sim-production-seed-host.js): closureContracts() = ownerIdleContracts(...) plus the host observer checkpoint as the LAST contract, used for every in-run closeCurrentInstant and for the final settle, so every pure continuation drains before an instant is judged. Evidence: repeated in-process probe runs 0 UNBOUND refusals (previously every second run); escapes observed with a shared observer are PROMISE-type only, which formation-sim-production-transcript-determinism.test.js already treats as inert. No timer, timeout or unref change.

Correction to the 10:37 simulator decision note: the current scenario DOES starve the seed past its election timeout. Base (old runtime, seeded randomSource) already has node-1 take over all 6 groups (formed 20044); on raft-rs node-1 likewise leads every group (formed ~20003, quorum 10000, fifth join 20000, 0 gaps). So O2 applies here: raft-rs draws each election timeout from the binding's unseeded getrandom (no seed/min/max lever on CreateOpts; core is process-global), and the instant of the takeover, the raft_protocol segment counts (e.g. 10917/11437 vs 10920/11445 vs 10917/11398), whole-ms busy cascades (1182 vs 1188 on node-0), same-instant raft interleaving and closure-round counts vary run to run. Seed 7 vs 8 differ only in identities and raft counts. Decision (epic precedent option B, as already applied to the production-handoff and charged-seed-host witnesses): formation-sim-runner.test.js test 1 now holds exactly what the harness decides - report keys, scenario, fidelity, identities, formationStartedAtMs, quorumAtMs, fifthJoinAtMs, node ids/roles/owner sets, group ids - plus formation after the fifth join inside SCENARIO.deadlineMs with every group led; isolation witnesses A/C/D/B now hold the per-run attribution shape (zero attributed segments without an execution node, identical owner@node set, identical per-node charged-owner set) instead of byte/digest equality; E and F are unchanged. Cost: schedule repeatability of the simulator is no longer proven.
